transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-08
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Cascade Head of ML), Daniel Reyes (Cascade CTO), Samir Khan (Platform Eng)

Summary:
Priya: wants to run a 6-week POC to validate an LLM-based product search/assistant for 3 core flows: product lookup, recommendation re-rank, and structured Q&A over product specs. Success criteria include latency & accuracy targets, and a clear migration path to Dedicated or Private deployment. This call scoped integration points (OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDKs), benchmarks (replay + synthetic), workload sizing, and timelines.

Topics:
- Success criteria and metrics
- Workload sizing and concurrency targets
- Benchmark plan and artifacts
- Integration: SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling, structured output formats (JSON schema)
- Security: VPC, KMS, SOC2, SSO
- Next steps and owners

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, can we do quick intros? we have about an hour, is that still good?
[00:05] Priya: yep, should be great. I'm priya head of ML, i own models and the evaluation rubric.
[00:09] Daniel: daniel here, cto, i'll be watching infra and security constraints.
[00:12] Samir: samir platform, i'll handle networking and kms stuff.
[00:15] Maya: perfect. liam from our SE team will go through technical bits and benchmark plan, i'll cover commercial and next steps. liam over to you.
[00:22] Liam: cool thanks. quick high level: Redwood provides both an OpenAI-compatible API surface and native SDKs. the idea is you can point an existing OpenAI client to our endpoint and it should work with minimal code changes, and we also have first-class SDKs for node/python and examples for tool/function calling and structured json outputs.
[00:40] Priya: that's good to hear. our team already uses an openai-compatible wrapper in prod for embeddings and chat. main questions: how compatible are you with function calling, and can we get structured outputs that we can directly parse into our pipelines?
[00:49] Liam: yes, we support the function calling semantics and have a structured output guide. caveat is model-specific behavior — the output schema enforcement lives on the client side or you can enable Redwood's output filters which help enforce JSON shapes. there's also SDK helpers for prompt templates + response parsing.
[01:10] Samir: quick infra question — do you offer a private deployment? we have data residency and egress rules, ideally VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for keys.
[01:18] Maya: yes that's Redwood Private. for the POC we usually start hosted to iterate fast, then move to a Dedicated or Private pilot if network/security gates require it. Private supports vpc peering, customer KMS/HSM, and audit logs.
[01:30] Daniel: if we do hosted for the initial run, how do we handle data retention and logs? security is a big thing for procurement.
[01:36] Maya: we can enable short retention logs and provide access-controlled audit logs; we'll send the SOC2 and ISO pack. we also have enterprise SSO (saml/okta) and RBAC.
[01:44] Priya: excellent. now on success criteria, i'll flag what matters:
- latency: p95 token latency for generation path should be under 400ms for simple completions; for multi-step tool predicated flows we expect end-to-end p95 under 1.2s
- accuracy: for our re-rank task we want nDCG@10 improvement of at least 8% over baseline, and for structured QA we need 0.90+ strict accuracy on a set of curated prompts
- throughput: support burst to 40 req/s during peak for the assistant service and sustained 8-12 req/s for background batch embedding generation
- cost: aiming to not exceed $0.25 per 1k tokens in the POC run, want recommendations off the bat for quantized models if that helps

[02:30] Liam: those are clear. for throughput and latency we need to size GPU pools; can you share your expected request distribution — average tokens per request and typical concurrency?
[02:38] Priya: yes typical generation is 120 tokens median, but product spec QA can be longer up to 800 tokens; embeddings jobs are batched nightly with 50k docs, roughly 40 million tokens per month.
[02:49] Samir: concurrency: typical front-end concurrency is 20-25 active users which maps to roughly 30 concurrent requests during peak. but search re-rank runs a separate service with high qps.
[02:58] Liam: ok that helps. for POC we usually run three model variants — a high-accuracy larger model, a mid-sized cost/latency tradeoff, and a quantized faster model for stress testing. we will run two benchmark suites: 1) replay of your anonymized production traffic, 2) synthetic extreme-case load to validate autoscaling and p95 SLA.
[03:18] Priya: perfect. what tooling do you use for benchmarks? we have a Gatling-based harness but can also take your harness if it's OpenAPI compatible.
[03:26] Liam: we can provide a k6/JMeter harness and a python replay script that accepts JSONL of requests; it also supports OpenAI client replay via the OpenAI-compatible endpoint. we'll share a benchmark spreadsheet that shows token usage and cost projections per model.
[03:40] Daniel: on the integration side, we have backend services in python and node; minimal code changes are preferred. how good are your SDKs for function calling and streaming?
[03:48] Liam: SDKs have full streaming support, response chunks, and helper for function calling callbacks. the OpenAI-compatible endpoint supports both the classic completion/response and the chat+function calling endpoints. in our examples we show converting existing openai.ChatCompletion calls to our endpoint by swapping the base url and api key.
[04:05] Priya: how do you handle structured outputs? we need the model to return a fixed JSON schema for product metadata extraction. sometimes the model hallucinates fields.
[04:12] Liam: a few approaches — 1) strong prompt engineering + schema examples, 2) enable Redwood's response filters that reject non-conforming responses, 3) run a lightweight validator step in the SDK which will call the model again for correction or escalate to a fallback model. there's latency tradeoff for retries but it's safer.
[04:33] Priya: sounds good. what's the fallback model idea?
[04:36] Liam: if a mid-sized model produces invalid JSON, we can automatically failover to the larger model for that request or queue it for async repair. you can configure routing policies based on failure rates.
[04:46] Samir: on routing/policies — can we route traffic regionally? we have EU/NA customers and some data residency rules.
[04:51] Liam: yes we support smart routing by region and policy — you can pin models to regions and have automatic fallback to alternative variants if a pool is saturated.
[04:58] Daniel: procurement will want to know SLA numbers and the Dedicated pilot costs. Maya can you cover that?
[05:05] Maya: sure. for Dedicated we can share example sizing + monthly commit. typical POC pattern is 6 weeks: 2 weeks integration and smoke testing, 2 weeks replay/benchmark, 2 weeks pilot with production traffic at low percentage. if you need Private, timeline extends by 3-4 weeks for infra setup and security review. I'll include a cost comparison in the doc I'll send.
[05:30] Priya: that timeline is workable. for success criteria we will provide a small benchmark suite and a labeled eval set for re-rank. want to confirm: will you run the benchmarks or do we run and share results?
[05:41] Liam: we can do both. preferred is we run the initial harness with your redacted replay to ensure objective measurement, then you run a validation on your side. we'll give the exact scripts and instructions.
[05:51] Priya: perfect. any constraints for embedding batch sizes? we have 50k docs initially and want incremental updates nightly.
[05:58] Liam: typical approach is a dedicated batch job with batching window tuning; we can recommend batch sizes depending on latency/cost tradeoffs and provide suggestions to reduce tokenization overhead (e.g., chunking). Dedicated pools are useful for predictability here.
[06:12] Samir: KMS — we use AWS KMS. does Redwood Private support customer KMS integration?
[06:17] Maya: yes, Private supports cloud KMS like AWS and customer-managed keys. for hosted, we offer envelope encryption and a bring-your-own-key option on Dedicated in some tiers.
[06:27] Daniel: ok procurement will want SOC2 and pen test results; Samir you will coordinate with them.
[06:31] Samir: noted.
[06:34] Priya: about function/tool calling — our assistant will call internal product APIs to fetch inventory and pricing. are you able to limit outbound network calls from the model or provide a secure connector?
[06:43] Liam: we provide tool calling primitives; you host the tool endpoints and configure allowlists. for Private we can do tighter network isolation and egress policies. also we support signing of requests and short-lived tokens from runway to call internal tools.
[06:58] Priya: that answers my worries. on success metrics — for the re-rank we will use nDCG and precision@k, for QA we will have a labeled set. can you integrate your eval alerts into our slack or are those only in Redwood console?
[07:10] Maya: Redwood console has webhook integrations and can push alerts to slack; we also share eval CSV exports for offline analysis.
[07:20] Daniel: about compatibility — if we point our existing OpenAI client at your endpoint will streaming and function calling work without code changes?
[07:25] Liam: mostly yes, slight header differences: we accept the same request body shapes and streaming chunk formats; you just change the base url and the auth header to our API key, examples will be in the repo. we call out a couple of edge cases in the docs where model-specific params differ.
[07:40] Priya: model onboarding — will we be able to pin exact model versions and roll back if a model degrades?
[07:45] Liam: yes, you can pin versions and define rollout policies like canary and A/B. console supports automatic rollback based on quality regressions you define.
[07:54] Samir: how do you measure quality drift in the POC?
[07:57] Liam: we ingest eval prompts and track a baseline metric; we can set alerts if drift exceeds thresholds. also have regression diffs per prompt set.
[08:07] Priya: great. now let's outline the benchmark plan and timeline concretely so procurement has something to sign off on.
[08:12] Liam: proposed POC schedule: week 0-1 integration + SDK swap-in (hosted endpoint), week 2-3 replay/benchmark with three models (large/med/quantized), week 4 pilot small percent of traffic with monitoring, week 5-6 scale up and finalize decision. total 6 weeks. if you want Private, add 3-4 weeks for infra.
[08:33] Daniel: procurement prefers a fixed window for pilot; we'll go with 6 weeks hosted first and then decide.
[08:37] Maya: notes for deliverables: we will provide benchmark harness, security pack, cost model workbook, sample SDK snippets, and a runbook for go/no-go criteria.
[08:49] Priya: about cost model — can you give a rough estimate now for 50k docs embeddings and the described gen workload?
[08:55] Maya: roughly: embeddings batch ~ 40M tokens/month, generation ~ avg 120 tokens * 30 req/s peak but sustained lower. We'll deliver a detailed sheet but expect in POC $X-approx: embeddings cost and generation cost combined likely in low thousands monthly for hosted; Dedicated reduces per-token cost but requires commit. exacts in the spreadsheet.
[09:14] Samir: ok. final questions on observability — we need token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing. do you expose distributed traces?
[09:22] Liam: yes trace hooks and we can emit spans to your tracing backend via OTLP; console shows per-route latency and token billing breakdowns.
[09:31] Priya: fantastic. that covers most things. any risks we should call out?
[09:35] Liam: main risk areas: 1) JSON schema enforcement causing retries and latency overhead, 2) edge-case tokenization differences affecting scoring, 3) networking constraints for Private deploys delaying timeline.
[09:48] Daniel: we'll mitigate by starting hosted, get quick wins, then lock down Private only if required.
[09:53] Maya: great. let's capture explicit acceptance criteria for the POC so we can measure success.
[09:58] Priya: acceptance criteria draft:
- Integration: replace OpenAI base url with Redwood endpoint and run smoke tests within 1 week
- Latency: generation p95 under 400ms for simple flows, end-to-end under 1.2s for tool-calling flows
- Accuracy: re-rank nDCG@10 +8% vs baseline; QA strict accuracy >= 0.90 on labeled set
- Throughput: sustained 8-12 req/s online and burst to 40 req/s for spikes
- Security: SOC2 docs received and VPC/KMS approach validated

[10:20] Maya: we'll use that as the baseline. I'll put it in the next steps doc.
[10:25] Priya: ok when can we see the benchmark plan?
[10:28] Liam: i'll draft the benchmark plan today and share by monday EOD. it will include the replay script, the k6 harness, sample metrics to collect (p95, p99, throughput, token counts), and the cost projection.
[10:40] Daniel: final item — function calling for internal APIs: do you have rate limiting and allowlist capability per tool?
[10:45] Liam: yes per-tool allowlists, rate limits, and we can configure timeouts and retry policies.
[10:50] Maya: ok wrapping up — recap of next steps and owners.
[10:55] Priya: thanks everyone, excited to move forward.
[10:58] Maya: thanks all, we'll send the pack and calendar invites for the benchmarks.

End of call.
